    Daniel Tupou confirms career call after premiership win

    The veteran winger was weighing up a contract extension.

    By
    Scott Pryde
    -
    EDITOR | October 7, 2026 - 12:49pm
    2,603
    Listen to audio version of this article
    Sponsored by
    0:00 / 4:35
    Instaread

    Sydney Roosters veteran winger Daniel Tupou has confirmed his retirement in a double blow for the tri-colours.

    Tupou has been weighing up whether to play on or not for a number of months, but after winning the NRL premiership in a tense grand final against the Newcastle Knights on Sunday evening, Tupou has called time on a glittering career.

    “I've been thinking about this for a while, and I know the time is right for me to finish playing. It's hard to put into words what the Roosters have meant to me because this Club has been such a big part of my life,” Tupou said in a statement released by the club confirming his decision.

    Related Coverage

    • Details emerge as Spencer Leniu set to make immediate club swap
    • Why Mark Nawaqanitawase will be back in the NRL
    • Sydney Roosters’ front-rower wants to pursue NFL opportunity

    “I feel incredibly blessed. I came here as a young kid just hoping for an opportunity and I could never have imagined the journey that would follow or everything I would be fortunate enough to experience along the way."

    Tupou's departure comes at a bad time for the Roosters, who have also lost Mark Nawaqanitawase for 2027 as he heads back to rugby union.

    The towering wing combination were the Roosters' biggest threat throughout the course of the year, and while the club have signed Reuben Garrick for next year, they missed out on the widely reported signing of Murray Taulagi who is instead heading to rugby union.

    Tupou's retirement, combined with Daly Cherry-Evans' departure for Hull FC, also creates something of an experience vacuum at Bondi Junction, with the defending premiers in a tricky spot ahead of next year.

    Tupou retires as one of the game's greatest ever wingers, racking up 198 tries in 307 games to sit third on the all-time list, while he is part of a 57-player club to have 300 games.

    Tupou won back-to-back premierships in 2018 and 2019, as well as the 2026 and 2013 wins.

    A one-club player, Tupou has been a stalwart of the Roosters for almost a decade and a half, and said it meant a lot for him to finish as a one-club player.

    “My faith has always been a really important part of who I am, and I'm grateful to God for the opportunities I've been given, the people He has placed in my life and for allowing me to play the game I love for as long as I have," Tupou said.

    “To have played my whole NRL career at one Club means a lot to me. The Roosters gave me my opportunity and this has become my home. To play more than 300 games, win four Premierships and share those moments with so many great teammates is something I'll always be proud of.

    “The Premierships are obviously very special, but when I look back, it's the people and all the memories we've shared together that I'll probably treasure the most. I've made friendships here that will last a lifetime.

    “I'm really grateful to all the coaches and staff who have helped me throughout my career, and to all of my teammates, past and present."

    Sydney Roosters head coach Trent Robinson labelled Tupou one of the greats.

    “When you look at what Daniel Tupou has achieved over 15 seasons, he will stand as one of the greats,” Robinson said.

    “But those numbers only tell part of the story of Toops and what he means to this Club.

    “Since he made his debut, he has represented what we want a Rooster to be. He has been incredibly consistent, selfless and dependable, and whenever there has been a big moment or a tough moment, he has been present.

    “Toops revolutionised the aerial game at the Sydney Roosters and became the greatest high-ball specialist of all time. He has always understood the importance of those early carries out of the backfield and the defensive plays on the end of the line.

    “He has never chased recognition. He has just turned up, worked hard, cared deeply about his teammates and represented the jersey with humility. That's why he is so respected by everyone who has played and worked alongside him.

    “To coach someone for virtually his entire career is very special. I've watched Toops grow from a young man finding his way in first grade into a husband, a father, a leader and one of the greatest players in the history of our Club.

    “We love Toops, we're incredibly proud of him, and his name will always hold a very special place in the history of the Sydney Roosters."

    Tupou, also played for New South Wales, Australia and Tonga throughout his glittering career.
